mission_05:
The **decoder block** is what makes transformers generative. Unlike the encoder (which sees all tokens), the decoder must generate tokens **one at a time** — it can only attend to tokens it has already produced.

The decoder has **three** sub-layers:
1. **Masked self-attention** — each token only attends to previous tokens (causal mask)
2. **Cross-attention** — decoder queries attend to encoder outputs (bridges understanding to generation)
3. **Feed-forward network** — same as encoder

The **causal mask** is an upper-triangular matrix of `-1e9` that zeros out future positions in the softmax. This ensures token at position i can only see tokens at positions 0..i.

Cross-attention is the magic bridge: the decoder uses its own queries to attend to the encoder's key-value pairs, effectively "reading" the source text while generating the translation.

GPT models use decoder-only architecture (no encoder), but the original transformer used both.
